Convert each series to MWh at its own cadence, aggregate separately, and report 100 times curtailed divided by available.

For California and Texas separately, find each region's highest actual hourly demand on October 19, 2026 local time, breaking ties by earliest UTC hour. Aggregate the two fuels before joining demand, and break ties by earliest UTC hour. For that winning hour, report average five-minute real-time HUB LMP minus matching day-ahead HUB LMP, in USD/MWh. Return all 21 combinations as columns iso_code, product, average_energy_price in USD/MWh. WITH hourly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('hour', interval_start_local) AS local_hour,
        avg(load_mw) AS hourly_demand_mw
    FROM core.fact_load_5min
    WHERE iso_id = 3
      AND CAST(interval_start_local AS DATE) = DATE '2026-10-19'
    GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', interval_start_local)
), changes AS (
    SELECT
        hourly_demand_mw - lag(hourly_demand_mw) OVER (ORDER BY local_hour) AS change_mw
    FROM hourly
)
SELECT max(change_mw) AS largest_positive_hour_to_hour_change_mw
FROM changes
WHERE change_mw > 0
